title: Gradual release flow for pinned model variants with gated canaries
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: When customers pin a model to a specific version we currently lack a safe, gradual path to promote a new micro-version or optimized variant behind that pin. Customers want to test new builds (quantized variants, kernel-tuned builds, or tiny architecture tweaks) with subsets of traffic without losing the safety of pins or requiring manual intervention.

Objective: Define and implement a gated canary / randomized A/B experiment flow that operates 'behind pins' — i.e., by default a customer sees their pinned version, but the platform can route a small, controlled fraction of eligible requests to a candidate version for evaluation. This must integrate with performance profile publishing, pin semantics, and the Console rollout UI and telemetry.

Requirements summary:
- Support percent-based gating on pinned models (0.1% -> 50%) with deterministic routing keys per request.
- Allow A/B experiments that compare candidate to pinned baseline on latency, cost-per-token, and quality metrics (eval-set pass rates / comparator functions).
- Expose promotion and rollback controls to Console and API; allow automatic promotion based on guardrail thresholds or manual promotion after N hours.
- Ensure telemetry surfaces per-variant profiles (perf profile publishing) and does not leak customer data.
- Honor customer-level overrides: enterprise customers must be able to opt out or require explicit approval.

Out of scope for this ticket: per-customer experiments that cross-tenant data, multi-region splitting logic, and implementing new comparator metrics (those will be follow-ups).
acceptance_criteria: Console: can create a gated canary target for a pinned model with percentage sliders and start/stop controls
API: PUT /pins/{pin_id}/canary accepts candidate_version, gate_percent, duration_hours, and auto_promote thresholds
Runtime: deterministic routing sends ~gate_percent of eligible requests to candidate; remainder continues to pinned baseline
Telemetry: perf profiles for candidate published under model-version namespace and visible in Console per-route performance panel
Safety: rollback triggers when latencies increase >20ms 95th or quality regression >5% on configured eval set
Security: gating respects customer opt-out and RBAC; feature behind feature-flag for early access
plan: Design: finalize API surface and Console UX (PM + Design) — 1 week
Engine: add canary routing layer which sits between pin resolution and model selection — implement deterministic hashing key and sampling — ENG-6391
Telemetry: publish per-version performance profile summary and link to existing perf profiling pipeline — ENG-6422
E2E tests: create a synthetic workload to validate routing percentages, rollback, and auto-promotion
Beta rollout: enable feature behind org-level feature flag and invite 3 existing enterprise customers
GA: flip feature flag and document in onboarding guides and changelog
telemetry_requirements: Per-variant time-series for: 95th latency, median latency, per-token cost, tokens/sec, error-rate
Evaluation metric capture: comparator result counts (pass/fail) against registered eval sets
Traffic attribution: which requests were included in canary vs baseline (hashed key) without logging PII
SLO alerts: auto-create a dedicated alert for canary runs > 1 hour with latency regression thresholds
rollout_policy: Min duration per step: 30 minutes or until N requests observed (configurable per org)
Auto-promote: candidate promotes when no regressions observed for 3 consecutive windows and 10000 requests
Auto-rollback: immediate rollback if safety guardrails triggered or manual revert in Console
Scope: canaries only apply to requests that resolve to the pin scope (org/project route). If request overrides model explicitly, respect override
notes: Deterministic routing: use request_hash(user_id || session_id || request_id) with salt derived from pin_id and candidate_version to avoid cross-experiment contamination
Edge case: when candidate version is not on compatible hardware, route back to baseline and surface capacity error in Console
Perf-profile publishing: publish a lightweight summary (json blob) to model registry rather than full profile to reduce noise
Security: security review required because canaries could be misused to exfiltrate behavior across versions — limit to org admins by default
